minutes.headline: Water commissioners declined to abate a resident's disputed high water bill, offering only a year of zero interest on the balance.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was a resident's appeal of high water bills at her home. The board held that water passing the meter is the customer's responsibility. It offered to waive interest for a year on the past-due balance and to test the meter, at the customer's cost if the meter proves accurate. The board also approved the annual meeting warrant with an added radio communications article, and heard the superintendent's report on a road repair, paving and PFAS pilot testing.

what_happened.line: The water commissioners offered a resident a year of zero interest on her past-due balance but did not abate her disputed bills; the vote was not audible.
The board held that water passing the meter is the customer's responsibility, and offered a meter test, paid by the customer if the meter proves accurate.
The board approved the annual meeting warrant, Articles 1-5 plus a new Article 6 for radio equipment from the cellular account; the vote was not audible.
Radio installation costs would be split three ways among water, fire and police, and the annual budget needs a two-thirds vote under the new bylaw.
The superintendent reported on a service leak, paving and a state permit extension, and limited PFAS pilot testing to the end of March.

why_it_matters: A water customer who disputes a high bill can expect the board to treat metered usage as the customer's responsibility, with interest relief and a meter test as the main options, and the test costs the customer if the meter reads accurately.
The radio article would draw on the cellular account and split costs among three departments, and the budget and warrant articles go to a vote at the annual meeting, where residents vote on them.
